definitions.explanation: The morning of the next day; the morning after a referenced event.

examples.japanese: {翌朝|よくあさ}、{彼|かれ}は{早|はや}く{起|お}きた。
examples.english: The next morning, he woke up early.

examples.japanese: {翌朝|よくあさ}にはもう{届|とど}いていた。
examples.english: It had already arrived by the next morning.

examples.japanese: {翌朝|よくあさ}の{出発|しゅっぱつ}に{備|そな}えて{早|はや}く{寝|ね}た。
examples.english: I went to bed early in preparation for the next morning's departure.

examples.japanese: {翌朝|よくあさ}{目|め}が{覚|さ}めると、{外|そと}は{雪|ゆき}で{真|ま}っ{白|しろ}だった。
examples.english: When I woke up the next morning, the outside was covered in white snow.

examples.japanese: {夜遅|よるおそ}くまで{飲|の}みすぎたせいで、{翌朝|よくあさ}は{頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}くてなかなか{起|お}きられなかった。
examples.english: Because I drank too much until late at night, the next morning I had a headache and could barely get up.

notes:
{翌朝|よくあさ} is a compound of {翌|よく} (next, following) + {朝|あさ} (morning). It refers to the morning after a previously mentioned event or time, and is primarily used in written or narrative contexts.

CONTRAST WITH {次|つぎ}の{朝|あさ}:
{翌朝|よくあさ} is more formal and literary. In casual speech, {次|つぎ}の{朝|あさ} or {明|あ}くる{朝|あさ} is used instead.

RELATED {翌|よく} COMPOUNDS:
- {翌日|よくじつ}: the following day
- {翌週|よくしゅう}: the following week
- {翌月|よくげつ}: the following month
- {翌年|よくとし}/{翌年|よくねん}: the following year

The {翌|よく} prefix always refers to the next instance relative to a past reference point, not relative to the present moment.
